title: Packaged tiers and credit conversion guidelines
author: Maya Chen
summary: This document defines a bundled pricing tier structure, conversion rules for legacy credits, and operational guidance for rolling the new packaged tiers out to customers. It includes concrete examples, acceptance criteria, rollout steps, and monitoring signals for the pricing launch.
overview: Background: As Redwood Inference expands Dedicated and Private offerings, we’re introducing a packaged tiers model that bundles reserved capacity credits, base API usage, and optional add-ons (observability retention, SLA upgrades). The intention is to make purchase decisions simpler for product teams while preserving unit economics and predictable revenue.
goals: 1) Provide clear, purchaseable bundles for SMB, Growth, and Enterprise that reduce sales friction. 2) Create deterministic migration rules for customers with legacy free credits or promotional credits. 3) Protect unit economics via explicit overage rules and burst pricing. 4) Give engineering/finance the telemetry needed to measure revenue and SLO impact post-launch.
pricing_model_summary: The packaged tiers combine three pricing primitives: (A) included token units (tokens), (B) reserved GPU-month credits for Dedicated capacity (reserved-credits), and (C) optional fixed-price add-ons (observability+, compliance+). Each tier lists included monthly tokens and reserved-credits. Usage beyond included tokens is charged at per-token rates; reserved-credits convert to compute-hours for Dedicated usage as described below.
tier_definitions_table:
| Tier | Monthly price (USD) | Included tokens (M) | Reserved-credits | Ideal customer |
|------|---------------------:|--------------------:|-----------------:|----------------|
| Starter | 199 | 5 | 0 | Individual devs / early prototypes |
| Growth | 3,499 | 150 | 1 reserved-GPU-month | Product teams with moderate throughput |
| Business | 15,000 | 1,000 | 3 reserved-GPU-months | Small enterprises and high-usage apps |
| Enterprise | Custom | 5,000+ | 10+ reserved-GPU-months | Large customers with SLAs and compliance needs |
credit_conversion_rules: Legacy promotional credits and free trial credits will be honored but converted to 'token-equivalents' on a fixed schedule. Conversion table: 1 USD equivalent = 1,000 token units for text gen workloads (baseline). Reserved-credits conversion: 1 reserved-GPU-month = 720 compute-hours; compute-hour consumption is drawn first from reserved-credits before billed as burst. Example: A customer with $2,000 legacy credit -> 2,000,000 token units; if migrating to Growth, any remaining token units apply against included tokens first, then overage rates apply.
overage_and_burst_pricing: - Token overage: billed at $0.00035 per token (text gen baseline). - Burst compute (Dedicated): when reserved-credits are exhausted, burst compute is billed at $12 / GPU-hour for on-demand V100-equivalent capacity. - Auto-burst threshold: customers may enable auto-burst with a 20% monthly budget cap. System notifies at 50%/80%/100% of burst budget.
dedicated_and_private_notes: - Dedicated reserved-credits are region- and SKU-specific. Migration to different GPU SKUs uses a performance-normalized conversion factor (e.g., A100-80GB = 1.8 * V100). - Private deployments are licensed as a platform fee plus option to purchase reserved compute; pricing for on-prem packaging is handled via enterprise contracts and custom quotes.
billing_examples: Example 1 (Growth): Growth subscription includes 150M tokens. Customer used 230M tokens in month. Calculation: 150M included -> 80M overage * $0.00035 = $28. Example 2 (Business with Dedicated): Business includes 3 reserved-GPU-months. Customer consumed 220 compute-hours. Reserved credits cover 216 hours (3*72). Burst billed for 4 hours * $12 = $48.
migration_plan: 1) Identify impacted customers via feature flag 'legacy-credit-holder' and export balances (Product/Finance). 2) Run a one-time conversion script to calculate token-equivalents and store as 'legacy_credit_balance' in billing table. 3) Notify customers with 30/14/7-day emails describing conversion and their new included balance. 4) Offer a temporary 10% discount on first 3 months when they switch to Growth/Business tiers. 5) Close migration window after 90 days and disable legacy billing path.
rollout_and_monitoring: Rollout: staged beta -> controlled release -> general availability. Stage 0 (internal beta): product, finance, sales test conversion scripts. Stage 1 (select customers): 50 customers across SMB/Growth/Enterprise for 4 weeks. Stage 2: regional rollouts (NA -> EU -> APAC). Monitoring signals: - Conversion success rate (target 99.5%) - Billing reconciliation delta (target <0.1% of AR) - Churn delta for migrated customers (monitored weekly) - Support volume (target <3x baseline after each phase)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Billing reconciliation tests pass for 100 synthetic accounts and sample customer exports. 2) Conversion notification content approved by legal and comms. 3) Telemetry pipelines emit new metrics: converted_credit_balance, tier_migration_event, burst_hour_charges. 4) Finance signs off on unit economics per tier (target gross margin >= 70% for Growth and above).
operational_playbook: If a customer reports a conversion discrepancy: 1) Escalate to Billing SME (finance-billing alias). 2) Pull ledger and conversion logs via billing-admin query. 3) If discrepancy > $1000, apply manual adjustment and create customer credit note. 4) Communicate resolution within 48 hours. Weekend SLA: acknowledge within 8 hours and resolve within 72 hours.
telemetry_and_kpis: Key telemetry: monthly_recurring_revenue_by_tier, avg_tokens_per_customer_by_tier, reserved_credit_utilization, burst_hour_spend, billing_disputes_count. Dashboards: Billing -> Pricing launch overview, Finance -> AR reconciliation, SRE -> Dedicated capacity utilization by tier.
faqs: Q: Will legacy free credits expire on conversion? A: No — they convert to token-equivalents and appear as a balance in billing. Q: Can customers split reserved-credits across regions? A: By default reserved-credits are region-scoped; cross-region conversion available via contract amendment. Q: Are tokens interchangeable between embeddings and text gen? A: Not 1:1 — embedding CPI is ~0.4x token baseline; conversion uses workload-specific multipliers.
